### Historical audit — S0139

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/generic_rsi/C2/development/commons_118588033/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines in this file. No reference or rendered image pixels are available in the supplied observations.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal — line 1 | The student was asked to reconstruct a 384 × 512 indoor photograph as separately editable SceneAct/Blender geometry, matching camera, framing, occlusion, colors and materials. A ship sleeping compartment is the student’s interpretation, not independently verified scene identity. |
| Build — lines 3–4 | The student supplied and executed a complete program with multiple assemblies: architecture, three-tier bunks, cabinets, lockers, chair, pillar, wall equipment, bench, pipes and lamps. It specified mattress surfaces, rails, supports, colored finishes, roughness and attempted procedural deck bump and lamp emission. These establish intended components and material operations, not their visual fidelity or successful physical connection. No articulated pose adjustment is shown. |
| Camera and lighting — lines 3–4 | The program specified a 25 mm lens, camera position and target, world illumination and four area lights. Whether framing, pose, lighting, texture assignment or occlusions matched the photograph cannot be established from code alone. |
| Validation — lines 5–7 | Execution step 1 reported `ok: true`, saved a render and Blender scene, and was selected in a recorded event. A subsequent request supplied the render and asked for visual comparison. This is technical render success, not independent geometric or visual verification. |
| Interruption — lines 8–10 | The second student CLI session exited 1; the trace records a model error and scene error but does not expose the referenced stderr contents. No comparison, revision, second execution or final student response is visible. The recorded selection does not establish final delivery after the error. |

**Teacher and autonomy.** No teacher message, detection, diagnosis, proposed update or teacher-directed execution appears. Therefore there is no evidence of teacher receipt or adoption. The student independently generated the initial scene, but the trace shows no successful autonomous post-render exploration; the attempted review was interrupted. The first CLI session reported zero tool calls (line 2).

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Classify this as a **successful initial build/render followed by technical interruption**, with final reconstruction quality and formal task outcome unknown—not an empty patch or demonstrated algorithm failure. Object names and the successful render log do not prove that parts meet, supports are plausible, materials were applied as intended, or the camera and lighting reproduce the image. The student’s landmark estimates and uncertain hidden supports are hypotheses (line 3), not measurements.

**Lessons.** Transferably, a saved render confirms execution but must be distinguished from visual validation, and a failed review cannot validate a revision. The particular bunk, pillar and fixture choices are task-specific hypotheses; their accuracy remains unresolved.
